per_request: The C bridge initializes a fresh reply for every request. A failed BusFault captures its request, completion, optional evidence and selected profile together with pre-callback CPU producer evidence. No global last-fault metadata is reused.
producer: For the detailed profile, completed writes snapshot in_instruction && using_restart && !mmu_restart && !exception_depth && !service_resuming. Restartable reads snapshot mmu_restart and a restart-aware instruction or initial fetch outside exception/service resumption. Both snapshots precede the callback; the public reply cannot claim CPU completion or restartability.
legacy: Old bool and precise callbacks retain their behavior and exclude the detailed callback on selection; resets and callback switches clear attachments while preserving required fault latches.
terminal: Detailed callback selection alone remains terminal and never falls back to legacy WB3/probe recovery. Separate physical read/write opt-ins may admit explicitly certified ExternalBus scalar requests with actual CPU producer evidence. All other failures remain terminal; qualified internal-RTE/exception-construction double-fault priority is retained.
metadata: Commit result is separate from explicit origin and whole-original-scalar no-commit evidence. Physical address is a CPU bus address, not a normalized backend decode index. Unknown/partial/missing evidence does not imply a frame stage.
limits: No WB1/WB2 frame, MMU, queue, IRQ, native, settings/default or installer behavior is enabled by this addition.
Malformed version/enum/bool or contradictory unknown/whole-no-commit reply causes the existing C boundary host-error latch, never guest frame generation.
Completed operations ignore structurally valid fault-only fields; they cannot leak into the next locally initialized reply.
scope: This document describes detailed callback selection alone; separate physical write/read opt-ins are governed by PHYSICAL-WRITEBACK-POLICY.json and PHYSICAL-READ-POLICY.json.
